yaw_rate_spike.classification: odometry-publisher startup transient; not the IMU acceleration filter and not genuine vessel yaw motion
evidence: The spike is read from OdometryPublisher twist and therefore is upstream of, and cannot be changed by, the observation-only acceleration filter.
The spike repeats with essentially identical magnitude when both, either one, or neither Surface plugin is loaded.

With Surface disabled and zero command, yaw pose is exactly constant while published odometry yaw rate reports -11.439907, -6.863944, -4.902817, and -3.813302 rad/s before becoming exactly zero at simulation time 0.6 s.
The filtered IMU and divergence samples have identical simulation timestamps, excluding the proposed filter-availability sampling offset.

surface_force_symmetry.source_behavior: VRX Surface computes one upward world-frame force independently at every configured body-frame point and calls Link::AddWorldForce at that point; it does not publish per-point force or torque telemetry.
surface_force_symmetry.conclusion: The two demi-hull buoyancy contributions are symmetric to the resolution of this test: removing either side produces nearly equal and opposite roll, while using both cancels roll by about three orders of magnitude. No Surface-dependent yaw impulse was detected.

stock_example_probe.conclusion: The pinned gz-sim/DART runtime publishes complete contact messages in Gazebo's stock contact_sensor world. The live Vehicle C contact failure is specific to the generated world or its sensor declaration, not a broad pinned-version failure.

topic_placement_ablation.method: In a disposable container, move only the stock example's <topic> element from inside <contact> to a sibling directly under <sensor>, matching the generated hull declaration.
topic_placement_ablation.conclusion: The generated topic placement is not honored by gz-sim 8.10. Nesting <topic> inside <contact> is required for the configured contact topic in this runtime.

closest_upstream_issue.difference: Issue 2037 reports Contacts messages whose depth, normal, and wrench arrays are empty; it does not report an advertised contact topic that emits zero messages. Its fix was merged in PR 2050.

contact_issue_search.conclusion: The stock Gazebo contact world publishes complete messages under the identical pinned image and DART runtime. A controlled topic-placement ablation reproduces the missing configured topic when <topic> is moved directly under <sensor>, confirming the generated SDF declaration as the cause. No production SDF change was made in this investigation.
